Your Dockerfile has FROM node:latest. Your docker-compose has restart: always and no health checks. Your images are 1.2GB because you're copying node_modules in the build stage. # Production stage FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs20-debian12 WORKDIR /app COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist COPY …

entry.summary:
A System-Oriented Approach to Scalable Hydrological Feature Engineering
Traditional watershed delineation wasn't designed for machine learning at scale. The standard approach treats each watershed as a complete, self-contained unit, which makes sense when you're studying individual rivers. But it creates real problems when you need to train models across hundreds of locations. We ran into this on a recent flood prediction project. The study area had almost no hydrological data, no stream gauges, no riverbed surveys, nothing you'd typically use for hydraulic modeling. So we trained an LSTM model to predict discharge instead.
